questions.q: What does the Judge decide about the second and third accused, Matthew Kumalo and Johannes Pafuri?
choices: They are found guilty of murder
Their guilt is 'not established', and they are discharged
They are found guilty of theft only
questions.explain: The Judge adds that their previous criminal association 'will be exhaustively investigated.'

questions.q: Why does the identification of Pafuri by the servant Mpiring fail to convince the court?
choices: Mpiring picked Pafuri from ten disguised men, but a tic is a 'marked characteristic' that can lead as easily to wrong identification as to right, especially with the face half-covered
Pafuri was not in the line-up
questions.explain: Identification 'depends on the recognition of a pattern, of a whole.'

questions.q: How does the court regard Baby Mkize as a witness?
choices: 'A most unsatisfactory witness' — confused, contradictory and frightened; her fear could have many causes
The best witness in the case
questions.explain: She had first lied to the police, saying she had not seen Absalom for a year.

questions.q: Why does the court accept that Absalom is telling the truth about the other two?
choices: Because he gave a straightforward account of his own actions and 'there seems no reason' for him to shield the real confederates and falsely implicate two innocent men
questions.explain: Yet 'previous association... is not in itself a proof of association in the grave crime.'

questions.q: What does the Judge say about administering an unjust law?
choices: A judge may bend it when society is unjust
'A Judge may not trifle with the Law because the society is defective' — if the law is unjust, it is the law and the society that must be changed
A judge should resign rather than apply it
questions.explain: It is 'the sacred duty of a Judge to administer it.'

questions.q: On what point does the Judge quote 'a great South African judge'?
choices: That an intention to kill 'may be inferred from the relevant circumstances', and is present where the object is grievous bodily harm calculated to cause death
questions.explain: The Judge cannot believe there was 'no intention to inflict grievous bodily harm' should the need arise.

questions.q: What is the verdict for Absalom?
choices: Guilty of the murder of Arthur Trevelyan Jarvis
questions.explain: The court finds his confession thoroughly investigated and true.

questions.q: Why does the Judge make no recommendation to mercy?
choices: He can 'find no extenuating circumstances' — a young man of manhood's age went to a house with two dangerous weapons, both of which were used
questions.explain: A higher authority, the Governor-General-in-Council, may still be merciful.

choices: That Absalom Kumalo be returned to custody 'and be hanged by the neck until you are dead'
questions.explain: 'And may the Lord have mercy upon your soul.'

questions.q: What breaks the courtroom custom as the broken Kumalo leaves?
choices: The young white man and Msimangu help him out, one on each side — white and black together, though 'white on one side, the black on the other' is the custom
The judge comes down to comfort him
questions.explain: 'It is only when there is a deep experience that such a custom is broken.'
